newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS AVOID ANY SLIPS TO STAY NINE CLEAR OF CELTIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS AVOID ANY SLIPS TO STAY NINE CLEAR OF CELTIC.

text.p: Rangers stayed nine points clear of Celtic in the Scottish premier division on Saturday when they beat Motherwell 3-1 and Hibernians 4-1 respectively.

The results left Rangers, seeking to equal Celtic's record haul of nine successive titles, top on 60 points followed by Celtic, who have a game in hand, second, on 51. Dundee United are a distant third on 39 after a 2-1 win at Hearts.

Rangers, who slipped to a 1-1 draw at lowly Kilmarnock during the week, made no mistakes against a Motherwell side also battling against the drop, going ahead through German Joerg Albertz after 20 minutes.
On the hour, Motherwell had a goal disallowed for offside, and Rangers broke upfield to go 2-0 ahead through Dane Brian Laudrup.

New Chilean striker Sebastian Rozental made his debut after 77 minutes and was involved in the move that led to Paul Gascoigne scoring his 17th goal of the season to put Rangers 3-1 ahead. Owen Coyle had given the home team some hope with a 68th minute penalty.

Celtic also had a convincing win over Hibs with unsettled Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooydonk scoring twice after 21 and 48 minutes, Brian McLaughlin struck after 42 minutes and Portugese striker Jorge Cadete added the fourth in the 68th. Kevin Harper got the visitors' goal in the 63rd minute and if Hibs 'keeper Jim Leighton had not been in inspired form, Celtic might have doubled their tally.
Dundee United consolidated their third position with their sixth successive win and their first at Tynecastle since 1985.

Swedish striker Kjell Olafsson scored his almost customary goal to put United ahead after 14 minutes before John Robertson pulled his side level with a 20-metre shot. Substitute Ray McKinnon cracked home an unstoppable shot eight minutes from time to give United the points.
